what.text: Anastrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor. Aromatase is the enzyme that turns testosterone and androstenedione into estradiol and estrone. Blocking it lowers estradiol in the blood. It does not affect the body's production of cortisol-type hormones or aldosterone.
It is FDA approved, as Arimidex 1 mg tablets, only for breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Using it in men, for example to lower estrogen or raise testosterone, is off-label.

items.text: anastrozole 1 mg tablets, taken by mouth.
compounded anastrozole capsules, 0.25 mg and 0.5 mg, taken by mouth. Arimidex comes only as a 1 mg tablet; compounded capsules are not FDA approved.

what.text: Anastrozole is approved for breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Its use in men is off-label.

research.text: Arimidex was approved on trials in postmenopausal women with breast cancer, including the ATAC trial against tamoxifen. In men, a handful of small randomized trials, from 12 weeks to 1 year, have measured hormones, bone, body composition and sexual function. The only trial in males on the label, in teenage boys, found no effect.
Human studies in men and boys

research.title: Older men with low or borderline testosterone (Leder et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
37 men aged 62 to 74 with screening testosterone under 350 ng/dL
anastrozole daily (12 men), anastrozole twice weekly (11) or placebo (14)
12 weeks
hormones, quality of life (SF-36), erectile function (IIEF), prostate symptoms, PSA, haematocrit

research.found: Total and bioavailable testosterone and LH rose; estradiol fell but stayed in the normal male range. Quality of life, erectile function, prostate symptom scores and haematocrit did not change. PSA rose in the twice-weekly group. The authors said the physical effects remained to be determined.

src.label: Leder et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab

research.title: One-year trial in older hypogonadal men (Burnett-Bowie et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, one academic center in Boston
88 men aged 60 and over with low or borderline-low testosterone and symptoms of hypogonadism
anastrozole daily or placebo
1 year
hormones, body composition (CT and DXA), strength, PSA, prostate symptoms, haematocrit, lipids; bone density and bone turnover in 69 men

research.found: Testosterone rose, peaking at month 3, and estradiol fell modestly. Body composition and strength did not change, nor did PSA, prostate symptoms, haematocrit or lipids. Spine bone density fell on anastrozole and rose on placebo (P = 0.0014); other sites moved the same way but not significantly. The authors concluded it does not improve skeletal health in these men.

src.label: Burnett-Bowie et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab

research.title: Anastrozole vs testosterone gel vs placebo in older men (Dias et al.)

facts.v: proof-of-concept, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, one center (US National Institute on Aging)
43 men aged 65 to 82 with total testosterone under 350 ng/dL: 16 on testosterone gel, 14 on anastrozole, 13 on placebo
12 months
lumbar spine bone density (main outcome), body composition, strength, gait speed, hormones

research.found: Both treatments raised testosterone above 500 ng/dL. Only testosterone gel improved spine bone density. Lean mass rose from baseline only in the anastrozole group; both groups improved knee strength from baseline. The authors concluded that converting testosterone to estrogen is needed to maintain bone in these men.

research.title: Anastrozole vs clomiphene in infertile men with low testosterone (Helo et al.)

facts.v: randomized, prospective, double-blind comparison (no placebo)
26 infertile men with testosterone under 350 ng/dL and normal LH
anastrozole or clomiphene citrate, both off-label
12 weeks
testosterone, free testosterone, estradiol, LH, FSH, SHBG, semen analysis, IIEF, erection hardness, ADAM questionnaire

research.found: Testosterone rose in both groups, more with clomiphene (mean rise 571 vs 408 ng/dL). Estradiol fell on anastrozole and rose on clomiphene. Neither group changed semen measures or questionnaire scores. The trial failed to show the two were equivalent.

src.label: Helo et al., J Sex Med

research.title: Pubertal gynecomastia in boys (Arimidex label)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, many centers
80 boys aged 11 to 18 with pubertal breast enlargement
6 months
share of boys with at least a 50% reduction in breast enlargement; breast volume, breast pain

research.found: No statistically significant difference from placebo. Estradiol fell 15.4% on anastrozole vs 4.5% on placebo. The label states efficacy in these boys has not been demonstrated.

research.text: Arimidex's approval for early breast cancer rests on the ATAC trial, which compared it with tamoxifen in postmenopausal women and followed them for a median of 10 years. These results do not tell us about effects in men.

In rats, anastrozole caused embryo-fetal toxicity at exposures 9 times the human level; in rabbits it caused pregnancy failure at 16 or more times the human dose. In female animals it may impair fertility.

us.text: Anastrozole is FDA approved as Arimidex, first approved on December 27, 1995, for breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Every approved use is in postmenopausal women; use in men is off-label. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: NDA 020541, a new molecular entity, approved December 27, 1995. It is a 1 mg tablet, now distributed by ANI Pharmaceuticals.

add-on (adjuvant) treatment of hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer; first-line treatment of hormone receptor-positive or receptor-unknown advanced breast cancer; and advanced breast cancer that progressed on tamoxifen. All are in postmenopausal women.
off-label. Men are not in any approved indication. The label says efficacy has not been shown in teenage boys with gynecomastia.

under section 503A, pharmacies may only compound with bulk substances that meet a USP or NF monograph, are part of an FDA-approved drug, or are on FDA's 503A bulks list. Anastrozole is the active ingredient of FDA-approved Arimidex. A compounded anastrozole product is not FDA approved.

world.lead: Anastrozole is an approved breast cancer medicine in the US, Canada, the UK and the EU, in every case for postmenopausal women. Use in men is off-label everywhere checked. It is banned in sport at all times.

after.text: Australia's Poisons Standard (June 2026) lists anastrozole in Schedule 4 (prescription only). Its ARTG registration could not be checked.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Anastrozole is named under class S4.1, aromatase inhibitors, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. S4 is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition). The list's S4 text applies to all athletes; it does not limit the ban to men. S4.1 substances are Specified Substances. Anastrozole stays named in S4.1 on the 2027 list, in force January 1, 2027.

side.text: The label's side effects come from trials in postmenopausal women. They include bone loss and fractures, heart events in women with heart disease, higher cholesterol, and rare serious skin, allergic and liver reactions. The small trials in men add bone loss in one.

items.text: in the ATAC bone substudy, spine and hip bone density fell at 12 and 24 months on Arimidex and rose on tamoxifen. The label advises considering bone density monitoring.
in ATAC, 10% of women on Arimidex had a fracture vs 7% on tamoxifen; spine, hip or wrist fractures were 4% vs 3%.
in women with existing ischaemic heart disease, ischaemic cardiovascular events occurred in 17% on Arimidex vs 10% on tamoxifen.
raised cholesterol was reported in 9% on Arimidex vs 3.5% on tamoxifen.

hot flashes, weakness, arthritis, pain, joint pain, high blood pressure, depression, nausea and vomiting, rash, osteoporosis, fractures, back pain, insomnia, headache, bone pain, swelling of the legs, cough, shortness of breath, sore throat and lymphoedema.

skin reactions with lesions, ulcers or blisters (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome); allergic swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, and anaphylaxis; liver inflammation. After approval, tendon rupture, trigger finger and high blood calcium were also reported.
in a 1-year placebo-controlled trial, spine bone density fell on anastrozole and rose on placebo. In another 1-year trial, only testosterone gel, not anastrozole, improved spine bone density.

surprises: The WADA 2026 list bans anastrozole at all times for all athletes; nothing in the S4 text limits the ban to men.
Anastrozole is widely used in men on testosterone therapy, but every approved use, in the US, Canada, the UK and the EU, is for postmenopausal women; use in men is off-label.
The only trial in males on the FDA label, in teenage boys with breast enlargement, found no benefit over placebo.
In a 1-year trial in older men, anastrozole raised testosterone but did not change body composition or strength, and spine bone density fell compared with placebo.
